core_obligations: Set up the induction: assume the ranks are positive and induct on the sum of the ranks minus one; if all the bundles are invertible the identity morphism works (proof lines 8445-8448).

Split off an invertible quotient: for a bundle of rank greater than one pass to its projective bundle, where the pulled back bundle fits into a short exact sequence with an invertible quotient and the pullback is injective on Chow groups after any base change (proof lines 8449-8458).

Finish by the induction hypothesis: apply the induction hypothesis to the kernel bundle and the other pulled back bundles to get a morphism with the two required properties, and compose with the projective bundle projection, which gives the statement; the author leaves the remaining verifications to the reader (proof lines 8459-8463).
proof_roadmap: Induction setup and the base case (proof lines 8445-8448).
Projective bundle step splitting off an invertible quotient (proof lines 8449-8458).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for finitely many finite locally free modules on a locally finite type scheme, a projective flat morphism of some relative dimension along which the pullback is injective on Chow groups after any base change and under which each module acquires a filtration by invertible sheaves, with the corresponding injectivity on the bivariant theory (statement lines 8428-8443, tag 0F5F-adjacent). The proof is an induction on the sum of the ranks minus one: at each step it passes to the projective bundle of a bundle of rank greater than one, where an invertible quotient splits off and pullback is injective, and applies the induction hypothesis to the kernel and the remaining bundles. The induction with its bookkeeping of injectivity is the substance, so the claim is H2.
